title: Tenant segmentation leakage investigation + quick runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This doc captures a recently observed partial tenant segmentation failure in Private VPC deployments where control-plane reachability for a small subset of customer agents intermittently crossed tenant boundaries. Impact was limited: a single customer reported brief telemetry leakage (health check pings seen in adjacent tenant logs) and two private control-plane agents temporarily refused connections when aggressive egress filter changes were rolled. No user data exfiltration detected. This is a working investigation + a quick runbook draft for oncall triage.

High-level symptoms observed (first alert to mitigation):
- 2026-03-09 03:24 UTC: Pager alert from internal metric: controlplane-conn-errors spike (per-customer shard) — customers A & C surface increased CONNECT failures to cp-agent.
- 03:26 UTC: Customer A engineer reports intermittent 403-like responses proxied by customer firewall appliance.
- 03:30 UTC: Oncall observes cross-tenant health-check log lines from customer B appearing on agent-host for tenant A (log tails).
- 03:42 UTC: Rate-limited mitigation applied: temporarily disable the aggressive egress rule that was rolled out at 03:20 UTC. Errors drop to baseline by 03:49 UTC.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Reverted the last edge egress policy change (deployment id: jira-PD-2319-rollout-7) at 03:40 UTC.
- Reapplied a conservative rule set that pins established TCP flows and preserves path MTU handling (workaround: allow related/established state and ICMP fragmentation-needed).
- Activated emergency logging (pcap capture on cp-agg for 30m, increased logging level on customer-proxy-sockets).

Customer impact summary:
- Customer A: 5 min increased error rate, service degrade for background sync jobs (non-frontend).
- Customer B: observed health-check logs present on wrong netns for ~12 min due to delayed cleanup of conntrack entries during egress policy shift.
- No SSO/auth tokens were seen in cross-tenant logs.

Evidence collected:
- Conntrack dumps from host cp-agg-17 (attached to linked artifact) showing duplicate tuples with different tenant tags.
- iptables-save and nftables rules snapshot pre- and post-rollout.
- Packet capture: shows SYN/ACK flows for health-check probes that traverse unexpected veth namespaces when policy hit sequence mismatched.
- Audit log: rollout manifest includes an optimization step that replaced a 10-rule explicit allow into a condensed blob using hashed sets; rollback removed hashed sets.

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis (working):
- The egress policy rolling change introduced an ordering-sensitive optimization (hashed-set replacement) that, under early-apply race conditions across the control-plane agents, created a short window where conntrack entries were rewritten without proper tenant namespace annotation.
- The conntrack rewrite + aggressive nftables replacement path skipped the atomic swap and used a two-step update: flush -> load -> swap. During flush, transient entries were inherited by the default netns and picked up by adjacent tenant agent processes sharing the host kernel network namespace.
- A second contributing factor: the rollout tooling did not quiesce the user-space agent (cp-agent) before applying the kernel-level policy swap; cp-agent keeps a small in-memory map of flow -> tenant mapping and relied on netlink events that were missed during the transient state.

Why this is new/different from past incidents:
- Past incidents were mostly due to route flaps or BGP session restarts. This incident is a kernel conntrack / policy application ordering problem that only manifests when dense hashed-set optimization is used and when multiple tenants have similar ephemeral port/tuple patterns.

Runbook (quick triage + mitigation steps) - DRAFT:
This is a pragmatic checklist for oncall to stop bleeding and collect required artifacts. We should later turn into an automated playbook.
1) Initial triage (0-5 min)
   - Confirm alert source and affected tenant(s) in Sentry/observability dashboard.
   - Check recent policy-rollout commits: run `git log -n 5 infra/egress-policies` and `kubectl get rollout rollout-name -o yaml` for staged operations.
   - If rollout present in last 30m, pause further rollouts: `infra-rollout ctrl pause --selector=egress-optimization`.
2) Temporary containment (5-15 min)
   - Revert to conservative rule set: `ssh root@cp-agg-N; iptables-restore < /etc/iptables/conservative.rules` (or equivalent nft command).
   - Ensure conntrack cleanup command executed per-tenant after revert: `conntrack -F -s <tenant-subnet>` (note: test on staging first).
   - If unable to revert, apply traffic isolation: rate-limit cross-namespace traffic using tc filters so that abnormal probes are dropped but established flows persist.
3) Evidence capture (parallel)
   - Start limited pcap on cp-agg host: `tcpdump -i bond0 host <customer-ip> -w /tmp/pcap-<tenant>-$(date +%s).pcap` (rotate after 5m).
   - Dump conntrack table: `conntrack -L > /tmp/conntrack-$(date +%s).txt` and save namespaced netstat.
4) Root-cause narrowing (15-60 min)
   - Compare nftables/iptables snapshots pre/post (we push snapshots as artifacts).
   - Check cp-agent logs for missed netlink open/close events; grep for 'netlink error' or 'rate exceeded' between 03:15-03:50 UTC.
   - Reproduce in staging: apply hashed-set optimized policy while running synthetic health-checks from multiple tenant VMs with similar 5-tuple patterns. Observe if conntrack tuples carry tenant IDs.
5) Recovery validation (30-90 min)
   - Observe zero cross-tenant log lines for 30m after mitigation.
   - Run targeted synthetic checks for customers impacted.

Operational action items (short-term):
- Immediately: add atomic swap mechanism for kernel-level policy replacement (PATCH: infra/patches/142) — avoids flush -> load windows. (Owner: Arjun)
- Add pre-flight quiesce in rollout tooling to signal cp-agent to drain flow-cache before applying kernel changes (Owner: Ben).
- Add a post-apply verification that ensures conntrack entries for the affected subnet are annotated with tenant metadata (Owner: Sofia).
- Expand observability: surface conntrack delta metrics and a per-host tenant-entropy metric in Console (PM sync needed).

Longer-term design notes:
- Revisit the decision to use hashed-set blob replacement in kernel policies; explore a versioned kernel map approach that allows atomic rename semantics.
- Consider moving tenant flow-annotation logic into a kernel-level module (or eBPF) that is resilient to netfilter reloads.
- Design a canary rollout that simulates conntrack churn before enabling hashed optimized sets across >5 tenants on same host.

Postmortem hypothesis tests to run (owner + timeline):
- Reproduce in staging with two tenants producing nominally identical ephemeral port patterns within 60s window (Ben, 3d).
- Run a controlled upgrade where we instrument conntrack to record source of entry creation and verify deterministic namespace tagging (Sofia, 2d).
- Load test cp-agent netlink event queue under rollout to measure missed events (Arjun, 1d).

Notes from oncall debrief (freeform):
- We saw gap between policy apply and cp-agent awareness; cp-agent log timestamps align with netfilter reloads showing ~7-12s of noisy transitional state.
- Customer B's firewall appliance also had an optimization that collapsed similar health checks into a single probe. This amplified the race window.
- We'll need to coordinate with customer success before any future policy format change — they run appliances with less strict namespace separation and may surface side effects early.

Open questions (still unresolved):
- Can conntrack entries be annotated deterministically at creation time, even when the kernel-level policy changes?
- Should we shift to eBPF for flow annotation to reduce reliance on netlink events?
- Are there other rollout tools that already perform atomic kernel map swaps we can borrow?

Appendix: useful commands and artifact locations
- Conntrack dump: /var/log/ops/artifacts/conntrack/cp-agg-17-20260310.txt
- pcap: /var/log/ops/pcaps/tenant-a-20260310-0328.pcap
- nftables snapshots: /var/log/ops/policies/nft-snap-20260310-before.txt and -after.txt
- Quick iptables revert command (conservative): `iptables-restore < /etc/iptables/keep-established-allow.rules`
- Quick check for cross-tenant logs (one-liner): `rg "tenant_id=\"[A-Z0-9]+\"" /var/log/agents/* | cut -d' ' -f1 | uniq -c | sort -rn`

Next steps for this doc:
- Convert this into a proper runbook entry under Console -> Runbooks -> Private Deployments / Network Policy Bleed (ticket to create).
- Schedule postmortem meeting with infra, sre, applied-ml (to understand traffic shape), and solutions-eng (customer appliance behavior) week of 2026-03-22.

If you're reviewing: please add notes inline especially if you have logs or pcap traces I missed. This is a working draft — will migrate to a canonical postmortem once reproduction runs and patch PRs land.

-- Maya
